title: Your live onboarding guide
subtitle: One conversation, one real project, one useful AI contribution. Keep this beside your friend’s shared screen.

stages.title: Before the call
stages.say: We will give your AI enough context to find something useful to do for a project you care about, then keep the result somewhere you own. You do not need to arrive with an AI task in mind.
actions: Book about 75 minutes; installations may need another session. Send the participant guide through your usual agreed channel before the call. Meet chat alone is not a durable handoff for every guest.
Open this runbook on your computer. Click New call, enter their GitHub handle and chosen notebook repository name when known. Keep the guide beside Meet; the friend shares their screen.

Ask the friend to sign in to GitHub and an AI they already use. Invite them to install GitHub Desktop, Obsidian, and system Git using the official links in the participant guide. No new paid AI account is required.
Have them bring a few non-sensitive sentences about one real project: desired outcome, current situation, decisions already made, and boundaries. They need not identify an AI task.
If they already have a notebook, reuse it. Inspect its rules and layout first; do not replace files or copy a second system over it.
stages.see: The friend has the participant-guide link and understands the purpose. Missing software is a reason to choose the browser path, not to cancel the useful part.

send.label: Advance message
send.text: For our call, bring one project you care about and a few non-sensitive sentences about where it stands. You don't need to know what to ask AI to do. Please sign in to GitHub and the AI you already use. Setup and download links: https://github.com/itsadoor-llc/second-brain-starter/blob/ai/friends-onboarding/onboarding/FRIEND.md — bookmark this; we'll use it after the call too.

recovery.action: Join the call and use the browser path. Aim for a useful saved contribution; arrange local setup later if needed.

live.purpose: Get your own guide and their participant page ready before anyone joins.
live.transition: When your friend joins, move to Get a shared view.

steps.say: Bring one project you care about. You don’t need to know what to ask AI to do.
steps.action: Copy the Advance message below and send it through your usual agreed channel. Suggest 10–15 minutes of preparation; reserve about 75 minutes for the call.
steps.see: Your friend has the participant link and knows preparation is optional.

steps.say: This page is my guide; the shorter page is yours to keep.
steps.action: Keep this guide beside Meet. Open the participant guide in another tab. Use Start a new call for a new friend. Have your friend’s shared screen occupy most of your display.
steps.see: You can glance at one instruction here while still watching their screen.

steps.say: We’ll keep the setup light enough to get to something useful today.
steps.action: Keep two limits in mind: five minutes stuck on one setup problem, and the final 25 minutes protected for the AI contribution, review, and handoff. If needed, use the browser path.
steps.see: You know where to simplify the call without pretending unfinished setup is complete.

stages.title: Get a shared view
stages.say: You will do the clicks. I will describe one step, then wait until we can both see the result. Stop sharing whenever you enter credentials. Today's aim is useful work you didn't have to invent for the AI.
actions: Join Meet normally with microphone. Then the friend selects Present now → A window or Your entire screen → the appropriate surface → Share. A Chrome tab works for browser-only steps, but will not show Desktop or Obsidian.
Ask them to describe what they see when a menu differs. Name the app, visible label, and expected result; avoid chains of instructions or 'click over there'.
Close unrelated tabs and notifications. Stop presenting for sign-in, passwords, recovery codes, or MFA; resume when the signed-in screen is ready.
Agree to switch to the browser route after five minutes stuck on one setup issue. Keep about 25 minutes for the project, contribution, and handoff.
stages.see: You can see the surface the friend is actually using, and hear each other. They remain in control throughout.

send.label: Participant guide
send.text: Keep this open and bookmark it: https://github.com/itsadoor-llc/second-brain-starter/blob/ai/friends-onboarding/onboarding/FRIEND.md

recovery.symptom: Sharing is blocked or shows only Meet
recovery.action: Choose the app window again. On Mac, screen-recording permission may need enabling and a browser restart; organization policy may block sharing. Continue with the participant guide and ask them to read visible labels if necessary.
Leave Companion mode if they used Present before joining. Rejoin normally, then present from inside the meeting.

live.purpose: Establish a comfortable pace and a view of the screen they control.
live.transition: Once you can see what they see: “Let’s make a place for your notes and the work the AI does.”

steps.say: You’ll do the clicks. I’ll give you one step at a time, and we’ll pause whenever something looks different.
steps.action: Welcome them and explain the goal: one real project, one useful contribution the AI chooses, and a saved result they can return to.
steps.see: They understand the purpose; they are not preparing for a technical exam.

steps.say: Can you choose Present now and share the window you’re using? If we move between apps, sharing your screen may be easier.
steps.action: They join Meet normally, then present a window or screen. Ask them to close unrelated windows and stop sharing whenever credentials appear.
steps.see: You can hear them and see their working surface, rather than an endless reflection of Meet.

steps.say: If a step gets frustrating, we’ll switch to the simpler route and keep going.
steps.action: Confirm they have the participant page open. Ask them to tell you the exact label they see if it differs from your instructions.
steps.see: Both of you have a shared pace and a way to recover from mismatched screens.

stages.title: Make their private notebook
stages.say: This is your copy of the notebook. GitHub stores it; Obsidian will be a convenient way to read and write the same files.
actions: Open the starter link. Select Use this template → Create a new repository. Choose their own account, a name such as second-brain, and Private. Create repository from template.

Confirm the page shows their account/name and Private. Enter those exact values in this facilitator guide. The template's root is the vault: Home.md and Profile.md are at the top level; there is no nested vault folder.
If an existing notebook already contains their work, use that repository and inspect its rules instead. Preserve its content. Adapt the project-note reference in prompts if its name differs.

The published main template currently has the older root layout. The new onboarding files live on this review branch until merged; use the participant link rather than expecting them in a freshly copied template.
stages.see: A private repository they own, with Home.md and Profile.md visible at its root.

recovery.symptom: No template button or name already taken
recovery.action: Check they are signed in and viewing the template repository. Reuse their existing copy or choose a new name; do not delete a repository to free a name.

recovery.symptom: GitHub account setup is blocking the call
recovery.action: Proceed with a local text note and chat-only contribution. Save the draft on their computer and record repository setup as unfinished; do not claim it is backed up.

live.purpose: Confirm whose notebook this is and avoid replacing existing work.
live.transition: “Now let’s choose the easiest way for you to write in it.”

steps.say: Do you already have a notebook repository you want to keep using?
steps.action: If yes, open it and inspect its rules and existing notes. Preserve it. If no, copy the Starter template link below and ask them to open it.
steps.see: You know whether you are reusing their notebook or creating their first copy.

steps.say: Choose Use this template, then Create a new repository. Select your account and make it Private.
steps.action: For a new copy, help them choose a name such as second-brain and create it. For an existing copy, just confirm the owner and visibility. Explain that a private repository still stores files on GitHub.
steps.see: Their account and repository name are visible. The new notebook says Private. Existing content has not been replaced.

steps.say: These are your files. Home and Profile are where we’ll start.
steps.action: Confirm Home.md and Profile.md at the repository root. Open Names for this call in your guide and enter their exact handle and repository name for the copyable prompts.
steps.see: The prompt previews point to their notebook. This version has no nested vault folder.

stages.title: Choose the writing surface
stages.say: We can use Obsidian today if setup is straightforward. The browser route still lets us experience the AI doing useful work.
actions: Local route: install system Git as well as GitHub Desktop and Obsidian. Desktop's embedded Git is not sufficient for the Obsidian Git plugin. On Mac, git --version in Terminal may offer the command line tools install; on Windows use the official Git installer.

Sign into Desktop while not sharing credentials. File → Clone repository → GitHub.com or URL → their repository. Pick a memorable local folder outside an existing repository or cloud-synced folder. Clone; note its exact location.

Obsidian → Manage vaults → Open folder as vault → the cloned repository root. Verify Home.md. If they accept the community-plugin trust prompt, enable the bundled Dataview and Git plugins; do not reinstall extra plugins.

Fill Profile.md: name, GitHub handle, exact repository, setup date, and their own boundaries. Open Projects.md; an empty rendered table is fine. Click the daily-note calendar icon and write one harmless line under Log.

Browser route: open Profile.md on GitHub → pencil/Edit → change the placeholders → Commit changes to main as the owner. Use Add file → Create new file for notes in the following steps. No Obsidian or automatic backup is established on this route.
stages.see: They can edit their own note on one chosen surface. In Obsidian, today's note appears and the project table renders; in the browser, their committed Profile.md is visible.

send.label: Official downloads
send.text:
GitHub Desktop: https://desktop.github.com/
Obsidian: https://obsidian.md/download
System Git: https://git-scm.com/downloads

recovery.symptom: An installer or permission issue takes over five minutes
recovery.action: Switch to browser editing and leave local setup for another session. Do not spend the contribution time troubleshooting.

recovery.symptom: Obsidian is empty or shows the wrong notes
recovery.action: Use Manage vaults → Open folder as vault and select the clone containing Home.md and .obsidian. Do not create another vault inside it.
Check Settings → Community plugins → Dataview. If they do not want community plugins, read notes directly and use Desktop or browser saving.

live.purpose: Choose one writing surface. Use the browser if installation starts consuming the call.
live.transition: “Before we add project context, let’s prove one small note is really saved.”

steps.say: Are GitHub Desktop, Obsidian, and Git already installed? If not, we can use the browser today.
steps.action: Use the official download links below if installation is straightforward. System Git is separate from Desktop’s embedded Git. If blocked for five minutes, choose the browser route and leave local setup for later.
steps.see: You have chosen Obsidian or browser editing for this call.

steps.say: Let’s open your notebook in the place you’ll write.
steps.action: Obsidian route: in Desktop choose File → Clone repository, select their notebook, and choose a memorable local folder outside other repos or cloud-sync folders. Browser route: open Profile.md on GitHub and choose the pencil/Edit button.
steps.see: Local route: Desktop shows the cloned notebook. Browser route: Profile.md is open for editing.

steps.say: Obsidian opens the same folder Desktop just downloaded.
steps.action: Local route: Obsidian → Manage vaults → Open folder as vault → the clone containing Home.md. Explain the bundled community plugins; if they accept them, enable Dataview and Git. Browser route: skip this action and continue.
steps.see: Local route: Home.md is visible in Obsidian. They understand and choose whether to enable the plugins.

steps.say: Let’s put your name and your own boundaries in your profile.
steps.action: Have them fill Profile.md: name, GitHub handle, exact notebook repository, setup date, and their off-limits list. Leave unknowns unknown. Browser route: commit this owner-authored context to main.
steps.see: Their profile reflects their words and repository; no credentials or private information about other people was pasted.

steps.say: Write one harmless line we can recognize when we check the save.
steps.action: Obsidian route: click the calendar icon and add a line under Log in today’s note; open Projects.md and look for a rendered table. Browser route: use the profile edit you just committed as the test.
steps.see: There is one exact change you can look for on GitHub. An empty project table is fine.

stages.title: Prove where notes are saved
stages.say: Let's prove this one line reached GitHub. Signing in to Desktop does not necessarily sign in the Obsidian plugin.
actions: For Obsidian: open its command palette and search for the Git sync command (wording may be Commit-and-sync, Commit and sync, or Create backup). Run the available commit/push operation. Refresh the repository on GitHub and open today's note to verify the exact new line.

Only a successful plugin push verifies the plugin's system-Git credentials. A successful Desktop push proves the Desktop route. The configured ten-minute schedule is not proof an automatic backup has occurred; verify a later unprompted commit before calling automation confirmed.

If plugin authentication fails, disable the Git plugin in Settings → Community plugins to pause retries, and use Desktop: inspect the changed files → enter a summary → Commit to main → Push origin. Verify the line on GitHub. Record 'manual Desktop save' in the handoff.

If Git reports an unknown author, set identity in Desktop's Git settings (Mac: GitHub Desktop → Settings → Git; Windows: File → Options → Git). Native Git may still need separate configuration; switch to Desktop if unresolved.
For browser editing, reopen the committed file on GitHub and verify the exact line. Before the call ends, save any later edits through the same verified route.
stages.see: A specific note and line visible on GitHub, plus an accurate label: browser save, manual Desktop push, plugin push verified, or automatic backup independently observed.

recovery.symptom: Authentication asks for a token or keeps failing
recovery.action: Stop sharing. Do not dictate, paste, or collect tokens. Use Desktop/browser today; system-Git authentication is a separate follow-up using the official plugin documentation.

Stop editing and automatic Git activity. Keep both copies; do not force-push or discard changes. Save an external local copy of today's note and ask for targeted help. Continue the AI part with pasted text.

live.purpose: Verify a real save, and name the method that actually worked.
live.transition: “Now we have a place to keep things. Tell me about one project you want help with.”

steps.say: Let’s check that your new line reached GitHub.
steps.action: Obsidian route: open the command palette and run the available Git sync/backup operation. Browser route: reopen the committed Profile.md. In either case, open the actual file on GitHub.
steps.see: The exact line or profile edit is visible on GitHub—not merely a success indicator in an app.

steps.say: If the plugin isn’t signed in, we can save through Desktop today.
steps.action: Only if plugin push fails: disable the Git community plugin to stop retries. In Desktop inspect changes, enter a summary, Commit to main, then Push origin. Reopen the file on GitHub. Stop sharing for authentication.
steps.see: The saved content is visible, or you have preserved a local copy and explicitly left GitHub saving unfinished. On a conflict, stop and keep both copies.

steps.say: Your working save method today is [name the one you verified].
steps.action: Say the actual route: browser, manual Desktop push, or verified plugin push. Only call automatic backup verified after observing a later unprompted commit. Keep this wording for the final handoff.
steps.see: Your friend knows how to save again without relying on an untested promise.

stages.title: Bring one real project
stages.say: Tell me what you're trying to make happen and where things stand. You don't need to translate that into an AI task. We just need enough context for a useful choice.
actions: Create Current project.md in the notebook root using the copyable starter below. In Obsidian create a new note; in GitHub use Add file → Create new file. For an existing project note, link to it and use its real name in the prompts; do not overwrite it.

Have the friend replace the bracketed text in their own words. Capture only context needed for this session; leave unknowns unknown. Do not paste raw private documents or other people's private details.

The project can already have a repository, but creating another repository is optional. Keep repos: [] unless an existing repository should be linked. Choosing this project today does not declare it their highest priority.
Save the note using the verified route. On the browser route commit their owner-authored context to main. Read it back briefly and correct meaning before asking AI to act.
stages.see: A short, truthful project note with a desired outcome, current situation, existing decisions, and boundaries. The friend has not had to design an AI task.

send.label: Project note starter
send.text:
---
type: project
status: active
repos: []
---

# Current project

## Purpose
[What I want to make happen, and why it matters.]

## Current situation
[What exists, what has happened, and what is uncertain.]

## Progress would look like
[An observable improvement; not necessarily an AI task.]

## Decisions
[Decisions already made, or none recorded yet.]

## Boundaries
[What to preserve; what must not happen; what is off limits.]

## Log
[Today's date: this is the project I chose for the onboarding session.]

recovery.symptom: The friend feels they must describe their entire life
recovery.action: Narrow to one project and the few facts necessary for today. Broader profile and repository organization can grow later.

recovery.symptom: The note still contains blank placeholders
recovery.action: Resolve only the gap that changes what useful work would mean. Do not let AI treat placeholders as facts.

live.purpose: Capture their intention without making them design a task for AI.
live.transition: “That is enough to give the AI a direction. Let’s see what it understands and what it can contribute.”

steps.say: What is one project you’d like to move forward? What are you trying to make happen?
steps.action: Listen first. Open their existing project note, or create Current project.md using the Project note starter below. This is a choice for today, not a declaration of their highest priority.
steps.see: A real project and desired outcome are clear. You are not asking for an AI task.

steps.say: Where does it stand today, and what have you already decided?
steps.action: Have them add a few sentences to Current situation and Decisions. Use their words. If there is an existing note, preserve it and supply its name/link or text to the AI later.
steps.see: The note separates existing facts and decisions from open questions.

steps.say: What would useful progress look like? Is there anything you want the AI to leave alone?
steps.action: Fill Progress would look like and Boundaries. Keep only context needed for this session; do not import raw private documents. No separate project repository is needed.
steps.see: The note gives enough direction to choose useful work and enough boundaries to avoid an unwanted move.

steps.say: Let me read that back. Is that what you mean?
steps.action: Reflect the purpose and boundaries briefly. Let them correct the note, then save through the route you verified.
steps.see: The friend recognizes their own intention, and the AI will receive the corrected version.

stages.title: Let AI find and do useful work
stages.say: Now we will ask your AI to choose one small contribution and actually produce it. We will judge it by whether it helps your project, not by how impressive the setup looks.
actions: Open the friend's existing AI. Copy Check access first. Verify it names actual sources and correctly reflects the project and boundaries. A repository URL alone does not establish access.

If it cannot access the private repository, paste relevant non-sensitive text from AGENTS.md, Profile.md, Home.md, and Current project.md. Do not spend the call installing an unfamiliar connector or changing account access.

Copy Find useful work. The AI chooses and makes one bounded draft, research item, comparison, or preparatory artifact. If it only offers a menu, remind it that choosing and producing one contribution is the request.

For an AI working on local files, keep its branch work in a separate checkout/worktree. Pause Obsidian Git activity and avoid editing those files while it works. A branch does not isolate working files from Obsidian.

Let the friend react to the actual result. A useful correction is evidence; do not pressure them to call an irrelevant result valuable. If the choice was wrong, correct the project context and try one smaller contribution only if time permits.
stages.see: An actual project-specific contribution, its assumptions, and a truthful delivery state: unsaved chat draft, local file, or linked unmerged PR. No ongoing background worker has been configured.

recovery.action: Use pasted context and an unsaved Markdown draft. Repository write access is optional for this first experience.

recovery.symptom: AI cannot browse but proposes factual research
recovery.action: Have it choose work supported by supplied material, or explicitly mark the research gap. Do not accept invented current facts or citations.

recovery.symptom: No result by the time limit
recovery.action: Ask for the smallest useful partial artifact and the checkpoint prompt. Record what was actually produced and what remains; do not call a plan a completed contribution.

live.purpose: Let the AI choose and make one substantive contribution from their context.
live.transition: “Let’s look at what it made and decide whether you want to keep it.”

steps.say: Open the AI you already use. First we’ll check what it can actually see.
steps.action: Copy Check access below and have them paste it into their AI. Explicitly supply an existing project note if it has another name. If access is unavailable, paste only relevant non-sensitive rules, profile, and project text.
steps.see: The AI names actual sources it received and says honestly whether it can read or write the repository.

steps.say: Does that sound like your project and your boundaries?
steps.action: Read the AI’s short understanding together. Correct a meaningful misunderstanding before continuing. A pasted repository link is not proof of access.
steps.see: The AI has enough accurate context to act. If a crucial fact is missing, answer that one question.

steps.say: Now we’ll let it choose one small useful contribution and do it. You don’t need to come up with the task.
steps.action: Copy Find useful work below. They paste it to authorize one bounded contribution. If their AI will edit local files, first use a separate checkout and pause Obsidian Git activity; otherwise request chat-only output.
steps.see: The AI begins producing a project-specific result, rather than handing back only a menu or a plan.

steps.say: While it works, we can let it finish. We’ll judge the result when there is something to look at.
steps.action: Allow about 10–15 minutes. If it stalls or only proposes options, remind it to choose and produce the smallest useful artifact. If time runs out, use the checkpoint prompt in Leave a usable way back.
steps.see: An actual artifact is available, with a truthful state: unsaved chat draft, local file, or unmerged PR.

stages.title: Review and keep the result
stages.say: Does this help you move the project forward? Let's inspect what it actually contains, then keep the version you want.
actions: Use Understand the contribution if an explanation would help. Ask the friend to identify one useful part and any correction. AI self-review is assistance, not independent proof.

For a real PR, confirm the destination is their notebook and read Files changed as well as the summary. This first contribution should add the expected Markdown note, without unrelated plugin, access, or instruction changes. Verify key factual claims before relying on them.
If satisfied, the friend—not the AI—merges the PR. If not, leave it open and request a correction or keep it as a draft. Saving and agreement are different things.

For chat-only output: on GitHub choose Add file → Create new file, use its descriptive .md filename and type: note frontmatter, paste the reviewed Markdown. Commit changes → create a new branch such as me/first-contribution → Propose changes/Create pull request. Review then merge as owner. If time is short, save a local .md draft and clearly record that GitHub saving is unfinished.

After merging remotely, stop typing in Obsidian, ensure local owner edits are committed and pushed, then fetch/pull main using the verified Git route. Reopen the note and verify the merged content before resuming. If local edits conflict, preserve both and stop.
stages.see: The friend knows what the artifact does and where it lives. You can open its actual saved content or explicitly identify the unsaved/unmerged state.

recovery.symptom: The PR changes more than the promised artifact
recovery.action: Do not merge. Ask the AI to isolate the authorized contribution on a clean branch while preserving existing work.
Capture their correction in the project note. Keep or discard the draft by their choice; do not score setup completion as demonstrated value.

live.purpose: Help the friend judge and keep what is useful, without treating AI output as automatically correct.
live.transition: “Let’s make sure you can find this and pick things up again after today.”

steps.say: Does this help? What would you change before using it?
steps.action: Let them react before explaining for them. Use Understand the contribution below if helpful, supplying the actual artifact or PR. Correct important assumptions and check factual claims.
steps.see: The friend can name a useful part or a specific reason it missed. Their reaction does not have to be positive.

steps.say: Let’s keep the version you actually want.
steps.action: If there is a PR, open Files changed and confirm it contains the expected note in their notebook. For chat-only output with GitHub ready, follow Full stage notes below to save the reviewed Markdown on a new branch and propose a PR. Without a working account or repository, save a local .md draft and mark GitHub saving unfinished.
steps.see: The actual proposed content is visible. No unrelated plugin, instruction, account, or access changes are included.

steps.say: If you’re satisfied with these changes, you can merge them. If not, we can leave the draft open.
steps.action: The friend makes the decision and clicks merge. If time or setup blocks this, save a local Markdown draft and label it not yet saved to GitHub. Do not imply saving means agreement with every claim.
steps.see: You have an exact link or path and know whether it is merged, unmerged, or a local/chat draft.

steps.say: Let’s check the place you’ll open next time.
steps.action: If using Obsidian after a remote merge: stop typing, commit and push any owner edits, then fetch/pull main through the verified route. Open the new note. If anything conflicts, keep both copies and stop. Browser route: reopen the saved file.
steps.see: They can find the actual result. It is not stranded in an AI chat or a branch they do not know about.

stages.title: Leave a usable way back
stages.say: Next time, you can give the AI an update and ask it to find the next useful contribution. You don't need to invent a task. This starts when you ask; nothing is silently running after this call.
actions: Have the friend bookmark their notebook and participant guide. Point to the saved contribution and project note. Demonstrate where the Continue with useful initiative prompt lives; do not launch another session merely to tick a box.

Use Pause without losing the thread if useful. The friend appends its corrected text to the existing project's Log or a linked note and saves by the verified route. A future AI must read that note or receive its text.
Have them complete the short handoff below. Be exact about installed components, actual backup method, AI access, and unfinished setup. Recheck any edits made since the save test.

Ask one natural reflection: 'What did this take off your plate, and where did you still have to steer it?' Record their own view if they want. This is learning from the session, not proof that the audience hypothesis is validated.

After this experience, separate project repositories and the existing weekly-review prompt are optional next steps. Use System/New Project Recipe.md when needed; do not make extra repositories a prerequisite for value.
stages.see: They can find their context, result, and return prompt, and can say what is saved and what remains to set up.

send.label: End-of-call handoff
send.text:
My notebook: https://github.com/{{HANDLE}}/{{VAULT_REPO}}
My current project note: [link or local path]
My useful contribution: [link/path; saved, unmerged, or local/chat draft]
How I save today: [browser / Desktop commit + push / verified plugin push / observed automatic backup]
My AI can: [read/write repository / work locally / use pasted context only]
Still unfinished: [specific item, or none observed]
Next session: open the participant guide, use Continue with useful initiative, and supply the project note, last contribution, and any update.
Guide: https://github.com/itsadoor-llc/second-brain-starter/blob/ai/friends-onboarding/onboarding/FRIEND.md

recovery.symptom: Time runs out before the contribution or save
recovery.action: Use the checkpoint prompt, save the actual draft locally if needed, and name the unfinished step. Arrange any follow-up directly with the friend; this guide does not schedule it.

live.purpose: Leave the friend able to find their work, save, and start another useful session.
live.transition: Close the call when the friend knows where things are and what, if anything, is unfinished.

steps.say: Next time, you can give the AI an update and ask it to find the next useful contribution.
steps.action: Show Continue with useful initiative below and its location in their participant guide. They bookmark the guide and notebook. Explain that this starts when they ask; no ongoing background worker has been set up.
steps.see: They know how to return without inventing a new task or assuming the AI remembers everything.

steps.say: Let’s leave a few lines so next time starts from what really happened.
steps.action: Copy the End-of-call handoff below. Have them fill the real project/artifact links, save method, AI access, and unfinished items. Use Pause without losing the thread if useful; check its wording and append to the project Log or a linked note.
steps.see: The handoff distinguishes saved work, unmerged work, and unsaved drafts. A future AI must actually read or receive it.

steps.say: Can you show me where you’ll find the project and how you’ll save your next note?
steps.action: Let them demonstrate finding the note. Verify the final handoff edits reached the intended destination using today’s save method. Keep unfinished setup explicit.
steps.see: They can find their context and result, and know their working save route.

steps.say: What did this take off your plate, and where did you still have to steer it?
steps.action: Listen without defending the system. If they want, add their reaction to the project Log. Agree directly on any follow-up that is actually needed.
steps.see: You leave with their honest reaction and a usable stopping point—not an invented success claim.

prompts.title: 1 · Check access
prompts.hint: First establish what the AI can actually read. No writes.

prompts.title: 2 · Find useful work
prompts.hint: The friend authorizes one project contribution, selected and produced by the AI.

prompts.title: 3 · Understand the contribution
prompts.hint: Replace the bracketed artifact reference with the actual draft or PR link.

prompts.title: 4 · Continue with useful initiative
prompts.hint: For a later session. Replace the update placeholder and supply the previous contribution.

prompts.title: 5 · Pause without losing the thread
prompts.hint: Use when pausing; check the text and save it using the verified route.

sources.label: Google Meet: present during a meeting
